section.title: Introduction
section.p: The UUID module generates Universally Unique Identifiers (UUIDs) and converts them between their binary and text forms. A UUID is a 128-bit value which can be generated without consulting a central registry and which is statistically certain to differ from every other UUID. It is written in text as five groups of hexadecimal digits:

UUIDs are standardised in RFC 4122, which also defines the URN form urn:uuid:f81d4fae-7dec-11d0-a765-00a0c91e6bf6. The module provides the three forms of UUID which can be generated without further hardware or policy decisions - time-based, and the two name-based forms - and a system variable which returns a new time-based UUID each time it is read. Storing the identifiers it hands out, and deciding what an identifier names, belong to its clients.

section.title: Overview
section.p: The module offers three SWIs. generates a UUID, changes a UUID from one representation to another (and so also checks that a text form is well-formed), and tests two UUIDs, given in any representation, for equality or ordering. Clients which only need a fresh identifier as text can read the system variable UUID$Generate instead.
The interface of and , in which each value is described by a representation type and a pointer, is deliberately the same as that of MimeMap_Translate.

subsection.title: Representations
subsection.p: A UUID may be held in one of three representations. Every SWI which takes or returns a UUID is given the representation as a number, and a buffer of the size in the table.

value-table.value: Binary data block, 16 bytes, laid out as described below
Text, a zero-terminated string of 36 characters (37 bytes including the terminator) in the form xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
URN, a zero-terminated string of 45 characters (46 bytes including the terminator) in the form urn:uuid:xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx

subsection.p: The text and URN forms the module produces use lower case hexadecimal digits. Those it accepts may be in either case. The URN prefix is accepted in either case too, and in the URN form any of the hexadecimal digits may instead be written as a % followed by the two hexadecimal digits of the character, as RFC 2141 permits. The - separators must be present, in the positions shown, in both text forms.

subsection.title: Binary layout
subsection.p: The binary representation is the 16 bytes of the structure below. The first three fields are 32-bit and 16-bit integers held in the byte order of the processor (little-endian), so the binary form is not in the network byte order which RFC 4122 gives for the fields of a UUID. Convert the form with rather than by rearranging the bytes.

offset-table.offset: The low 32 bits of the time (the first group of digits of the text form)
The middle 16 bits of the time (the second group)
The high 12 bits of the time in bits 0-11, and the UUID version in bits 12-15 (the third group)
The high 6 bits of the clock sequence in bits 0-5, and the variant in bits 6-7, which is 2 (binary 10) for the UUIDs of RFC 4122 (the first two digits of the fourth group)
The low 8 bits of the clock sequence (the last two digits of the fourth group)
The node identifier, as six bytes in the order they are written in the text form (the fifth group)

subsection.p: For a name-based UUID the fields other than the version and variant bits are taken from the hash of the namespace and name, and have no meaning of their own.

subsection.title: UUID versions
subsection.p: The version of a UUID states how it was generated. It is held in the high four bits of time_hi_and_version and is chosen with bits 4-7 of the flags given to .

value-table.value: Time-based UUID, generated from the clock, a clock sequence and the node identifier
DCE security UUID. The module does not generate these
Name-based UUID, using the MD5 hash of a namespace and a name
Randomly generated UUID. The module does not generate these
Name-based UUID, using the SHA-1 hash of a namespace and a name

subsection.p: Requesting a version which the module does not generate, or a version outside this range, returns the error .

subsection.title: Time-based UUIDs
subsection.p: A time-based UUID is made from the time, a clock sequence, and a node identifier. The time is the system clock, counted in 100 nanosecond units since 15 October 1582 (although the clock does not have so fine a resolution). The node identifier is the Ethernet hardware address of the machine, if the system can supply one; otherwise it is a random value with the multicast bit set, as RFC 4122 recommends, which is chosen once and kept for as long as the module is running.

The clock sequence is chosen at random when the module has no record of an earlier UUID, or when the node identifier has changed, and is increased if the clock is found to have gone backwards. This keeps the UUIDs distinct if the clock is reset or the network hardware is changed. The module keeps the clock sequence, the time of the last UUID and the node identifier in the file UUID.State, which it reads from Choices: when it starts and writes back to <Choices$Write> when the module is finalised.

subsection.title: Name-based UUIDs
subsection.p: A name-based UUID is the same every time it is generated from the same namespace and name. This lets a tool or application be given a stable identifier from its name, with the namespace keeping names from different sources apart. The namespace is itself a UUID, given to in its binary representation. The name is a sequence of bytes, given either with a length or as a zero-terminated string.

RFC 4122 defines the namespace UUIDs for domain names, URLs, ISO object identifiers and X.500 names. The one for domain names is 6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8; the MD5 name-based UUID for the name www.example.com within it is 5df41881-3aed-3515-88a7-2f4a814cf09e.

section.title: SWI calls
section.p: The module allocates the SWI chunk UUID_ at &hex;582C0.

swi-definition.name: UUID_Convert
swi-definition.description: Converts a UUID from one representation to another

entry.register-use: Pointer to the UUID in the input representation
Pointer to a buffer to receive the UUID in the output representation

use.p: This SWI converts a UUID between the representations described in Technical details. The output buffer must be 16 bytes for the binary representation, 37 bytes for the text representation and 46 bytes for the URN representation. The input and output may use the same representation, in which case the SWI checks the text or URN form is well-formed and copies it.

The text and URN forms are checked as they are converted. The text form must be exactly 36 characters, the hexadecimal digits and the - separators in the places shown, and the URN form must begin with urn:uuid:. The input representation type must be 0, 1 or 2; the SWI does not check this, and the result for any other value is not defined.
If the output representation is not 0, 1 or 2 the error is returned. A malformed text string gives and a malformed URN gives .

swi-definition.name: UUID_Create
swi-definition.description: Creates a new Universally Unique Identifier

entry.register-use:
Flags:
Binary representation, 16 bytes Text representation, 37 bytes URN representation, 46 bytes
Time-based UUID Name-based UUID, using MD5 Name-based UUID, using SHA-1
Other values give an error.
Reserved, must be 0
Pointer to a buffer to receive the UUID, of the size for the representation
Name-based versions only: pointer to the namespace, as a UUID in the binary representation
Name-based versions only: pointer to the name
Name-based versions only: length of the name in bytes, or 0 if the name is a zero-terminated string

use.p: This SWI generates a new UUID and writes it, in the representation requested, to the buffer in R1. For a time-based UUID, R2 to R4 are not used and need not be valid.

For a name-based UUID the namespace is read from R2 as 16 bytes in the binary representation (use to make one from text). The name is read from R3. If R4 is 0 the name is the characters up to a terminating zero byte; otherwise it is the number of bytes in R4. A negative length returns the error .
A version which the module does not generate returns , and a representation other than 0, 1 or 2 returns . If a time-based UUID cannot be generated the error is returned.

value-table.value: The first UUID orders before the second
The first UUID orders after the second

use.p: This SWI compares two UUIDs, each of which may be in any representation, and need not be in the same one. The UUIDs are ordered by their fields in the order they are written in the text form, which is the order in which their text forms would sort. This ordering does not reflect the order in which the UUIDs were created.
Either UUID may return the errors of if it is a text or URN form which is not well-formed.

Reading this variable returns a new time-based UUID in the text representation, a string of 36 characters. It is a code variable, so every read generates a different value. Take a copy of the value before using it: reading the variable again, even to find its length, returns another UUID.
The variable cannot be set or deleted by a client; an attempt to write to it returns the error . It is created when the module starts and removed when the module is finalised.

section.title: Error messages
section.p: The module allocates the errors from &hex;81AFC0.

use.p: A time-based UUID could not be generated.

A URN given to or did not begin with urn:uuid:, was not followed by exactly 36 characters of UUID, or had a character in it which is not a hexadecimal digit, a correctly placed -, or a complete % escape of a hexadecimal digit.
A text UUID given to or was not 36 characters long, or had a character in it which is not a hexadecimal digit or a correctly placed -.
An attempt was made to set UUID$Generate.

subsection.title: Reading a new UUID from BASIC
subsection.p: A new time-based identifier is read from the system variable. The value is copied into a BASIC string before it is used.

subsection.title: Making a name-based UUID
subsection.p: A name-based UUID is made in a namespace given in its binary form, converted here from the text form of the domain name namespace.

subsection.title: Checking whether two UUIDs match
subsection.p: The two UUIDs may be held in different forms.
